subject: POC trial: clarify hosting preference & agree next steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Kelly <morgan.kelly@novamed.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial: clarify hosting preference & agree next steps

Thanks again for a productive call today — appreciate you walking us through the integration constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the PoC path: 

Recap / constraints you mentioned:
- Data residency: PHI-adjacent logs must remain in your VPC for the trial (Elena to confirm exact scope).
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 250ms for inference on typical 512-token prompts.
- TPS: Expect short bursts up to ~15 concurrent requests; baseline ~2-3 RPS.
- Compliance: You need audit logs and token retention controls visible to your security team.

Options that fit (summary):
1) Hosted API — fastest to start but requires us to route logs/metrics; may not meet your residency ask without Private.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pool in our infra; good middle ground for predictable throughput and easier audit access.
3) Private VPC/on-prem — full isolation and residency, longer lead time.

Proposed PoC (3 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): finalize which mode to test (hosted vs dedicated vs private), share minimal security checklist, and get stakeholder signoff.
- Week 1: Integration — implement a sample integration (SDK + few endpoints), verify KV caching and auth flows.
- Week 2: Load & regressions — run realistic workload, capture latency/cost metrics, exercise fallback routing.
- Week 3: Evaluation & handoff — review success criteria, ops runbook, recommended next steps.

Success criteria (suggested):
- Functional: End-to-end inference with expected output fidelity on 5 canonical prompts.
- Performance: 95th latency < 250ms; cold-start < 800ms.
- Reliability: 99% of requests succeed without retry in steady-state.
- Ops: Logs, KV cache traces, and audit events visible to your security team.

Ask from you now:
1) Confirm which deployment mode you want to trial (Hosted / Dedicated / Private). If Private, please confirm point of contact (Elena?).
2) Share a small set of 5 canonical prompts and an example request/response format for fidelity checks.
3) Confirm one infra and one product stakeholder for the trial.

Attached: redwood-deployment-options-one-pager.pdf (short summary)

Happy to jump on a 30m planning call early next week once you confirm mode.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

From: Morgan Kelly <morgan.kelly@novamed.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@novamed.com>
Cc: Elena Rios <elena.rios@novamed.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial: clarify hosting preference & agree next steps

Thanks Logan — this is helpful and captures the call. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Residency: Our security lead (Elena) needs the logs and audit events to never land in a third-party account; exporting metadata is fine if it remains inside our VPC. That rules out standard Hosted API unless theres a gateway option.
- Latency budget: 250ms 95th is tight; were willing to accept up to 300ms in the PoC but would prefer to hit <250ms if possible.
- Timeline: Were targeting a customer demo in mid-June, so a 3-week PoC that finishes by the end of May would be ideal. Is that feasible?

Action items from our side:
- I will send the 5 canonical prompts and example payloads by EOD Monday.
- Elena will confirm the exact residency scope (logs vs payload) and share the final contact.

For now, I think Dedicated capacity looks like the right tradeoff — gives us predictable performance and more control over audit exposure. But Elenas input may push us to Private.

—Morgan
Morgan Kelly
Senior Product Manager, NovaMed
morgan.kelly@novamed.com

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Kelly <morgan.kelly@novamed.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial: clarify hosting preference & agree next steps

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Morgan — Dedicated sounds like a pragmatic first step. To keep momentum, heres a concrete plan and ask: 

Immediate (this week)
- Please confirm Dedicated as the initial PoC mode (we can pivot to Private if Elena requires it).
- Share the 5 prompts + sample payloads (you mentioned EOD Monday).
- Confirm infra contact for network/firewall rules (well need a small set of egress IPs for the Dedicated fleet).

PoC charter doc attached: novamed-poc-charter.docx (includes roles, timeline, and minimal security checklist). Key owners: 
- NovaMed: Morgan (product), Elena (security/infra), Samir (project sponsor)
- Redwood: Logan (AE, PoC lead), Ben (Solutions Engineer), Marissa (Customer Success)

Measurement plan (we will share a dashboard):
- Latency percentiles, token counts & cost estimate, success rate, and sample output diffs against your canonical prompts.

Can Ben and I get 30 minutes Wednesday to walk through the charter and confirm IPs and access method? If Wednesday is tight, Thursday morning works.

Thanks — Ill hold a calendar placeholder for Wed 10:00am PT and send a short agenda; cancel if that conflicts.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Kelly <morgan.kelly@novamed.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@novamed.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial: clarify hosting preference & agree next steps

Looping in a couple quick notes from an ops/solution standpoint — quoted below for context.

> Dedicated fleet is a good mid-point; we can reserve capacity and provide static egress IPs. If youre OK with that, we can pre-provision and share firewall rules this week.
> 
> For audit/logging: we can forward audit events to your VPC via a secure connector (logs-only) while keeping model payloads isolated. 

Two practical asks from my side before we provision: 
1) Expected peak concurrency and any scheduled bulk jobs we should simulate. (You mentioned short bursts ~15 concurrently; confirm if thats per-region.)
2) Which model family or size you want to exercise in the PoC (we can mirror your prod candidate or pick a close Redwood-verified variant).

If Dedicated is confirmed, ops notes: provisioning lead time ~3 business days once we have firewall IPs and the infra contact approves the connector. Private/VPC adds ~3-4 weeks due to network approvals.

Ill join the charter call and map bench tests to your prompts.

—Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachments: none
